project.title: Tiny Village - MVP Delivery and Human Review
project.description: Ordered simulation delivery with issue-backed tasks, native dependencies, human phase gates, and explicit UX, UI, aesthetics, accessibility, and engineering reviews.

fields.name: Phase
options: 02 Freeze MVP, dependencies, and design foundations
04 Align actions, world state, and GOAP
08 Validate UX, UI, aesthetics, and MVP release

1.name: Restore reliable startup
1.outcome: Fresh-process startup and graph initialization complete without import errors, deadlocks, or unsafe shared-cache handling.

2.name: Freeze MVP, dependencies, and design foundations
2.outcome: A maintainer approves MVP scope, reproducible CPU setup, CI, user journeys, visual direction, and engineering constraints.

3.name: Consolidate backlog and pull requests
3.outcome: Every original backlog item has an evidence-based disposition, and the selected PR queue has current owners and prerequisites.

4.name: Align actions, world state, and GOAP
4.outcome: Real characters execute complete plans across ticks with consistent state, bounded replanning, and correct target resolution.

5.name: Complete event-driven execution
5.outcome: Events affect the intended actor and update state, memory, and accounting once while isolating failures.

6.name: Deliver the village economic loop
6.outcome: Work, wages, production, trade, consumption, and recovery form one demonstrable behavior loop.

7.name: Restore saved simulation state
7.outcome: A versioned save/restart/load round trip preserves world identity and subsequent simulation behavior.

8.name: Validate UX, UI, aesthetics, and MVP release
8.outcome: Documented demo, visual and accessibility reviews, engineering review, and measured stability have human sign-off.

9.name: Expand optional features deliberately
9.outcome: Post-MVP social, memory, LLM, and graphics increments have verified fallbacks and an explicit human release decision.

items.title: Tiny Village: ordered MVP delivery and human review program
items.goal: Deliver the approved nine-phase roadmap through issue-backed work, native dependencies, human phase decisions, and explicit design reviews.
acceptance: Every work item and review has a repository issue and Project row.
Phase, Sequence, Readiness, Scope, Depends on, Review owner, and Decision communicate execution order.
A phase cannot advance until its human gate records Approved; no automated process approves a gate.
MVP release is Phase 8; Phase 9 and optional tasks do not block the Phase 8 release.

items.title: Phase 1: Restore reliable startup
items.goal: Fresh-process startup and graph initialization complete without import errors, deadlocks, or unsafe shared-cache handling.
acceptance: All phase work is tracked as individual issues.
Phase gate H1 records the human decision and evidence.
Optional/deferred work is explicitly documented and does not silently become a release prerequisite.

items.title: Fix Goal fallback import failure and validate PR #706
items.goal: Remove the unreachable fallback handler in tiny_utility_functions.py and prove cold imports work.
acceptance: Rebase/review PR #706 against current main, retaining real fallback behavior.
Run main.py minimal/test entry points and GOAP imports in fresh subprocesses with timeouts.
Report passing, failing, skipped, and unexecuted checks distinctly.

items.title: Remove recursive global GraphManager initialization deadlock
items.goal: Eliminate the reproduced lock re-entry: graph import constructs character/event/action objects that call get_global_graph_manager while its non-reentrant lock is held.
acceptance: Remove import-time world construction and explicitly wire graph ownership.
Reproduce and resolve the named-target initialization hang; do not merely swap locks without checking recursive initialization.
Fresh-process import-order and singleton checks complete within a bounded timeout and return the same graph instance.

items.title: Use an owned cache directory and safely validate PR #701
items.goal: Replace world-writable temporary cache handling with a supported directory owned by the runtime user.
acceptance: Review PR #701 and verify cache ownership, permissions, and repeat startup.
Exclude the repro_check.py script that deletes an existing shared cache; use an isolated temporary fixture.
Preserve TLS/checksum verification and avoid importing models solely to initialize a cache.

items.title: Human engineering review: startup, imports, and graph lifecycle
items.goal: A maintainer reviews the startup repairs and their evidence before approving broader development.
acceptance: Walk through both reproduced blockers and inspect the repairs at their current commit SHA.
Check dependency injection, graph ownership, thread initialization, import side effects, and error propagation.
Record Approved, Changes requested, or Deferred with reviewer identity, rationale, evidence, and follow-up issues.

items.title: Human decision gate 1: Restore reliable startup
items.goal: A human maintainer decides whether the phase satisfies its acceptance criteria and may unlock the next phase.
acceptance: Review every required task, current PR head, commands/results, and the phase-specific evidence.
Walk through the supported behavior, failure cases, and applicable design/engineering artifacts.
Choose exactly Approved, Changes requested, or Deferred; record reviewer, date, rationale, evidence, and issue-backed remediation.
Only close this gate after a human records Approved; keep rework/deferred gates open and downstream work blocked.
Do not auto-approve based on a passing suite, a bot action, elapsed time, or a completed checklist.

items.title: Phase 2: Freeze MVP, dependencies, and design foundations
items.goal: A maintainer approves MVP scope, reproducible CPU setup, CI, user journeys, visual direction, and engineering constraints.
acceptance: All phase work is tracked as individual issues.
Phase gate H2 records the human decision and evidence.
Optional/deferred work is explicitly documented and does not silently become a release prerequisite.

items.title: Define the MVP scenario, support matrix, and release budgets
items.goal: Specify fixed villagers, simulation ticks/events, the canonical headless command, visible state changes, supported visual surfaces, and measurable budgets.
acceptance: Define the work/earn/acquire-food/eat/recover scenario with fixed seed and deterministic inputs.
Decide supported console and Pygame user flows and explicitly defer unrelated quests, VR, multiplayer, and tooling.
Agree latency, frame-time, memory, stability, and review evidence requirements without inventing delivery dates.

items.title: Provide repository-supported core dependencies and optional ML extras
items.goal: Turn the tested cloud setup into reproducible repository-supported Python 3.12 installation profiles.
acceptance: Define and lock core runtime/development dependencies separately from optional GPU, NLP, and LLM packages.
Review PR #704 so optional FAISS is not an entry-point requirement.
Validate clean installation and repeat installation with artifact and TLS verification enabled.

items.title: Make the minimal demo independent of heavy and graphics initialization
items.goal: Complete the existing lightweight-demo issue with real runtime boundaries instead of global sys.modules patches.
acceptance: Minimal mode works without display initialization, model downloads, and optional pygame/NLP/LLM dependencies.
Separate renderer/model initialization from simulation construction using repository-supported interfaces.
Optional dependency failure is observable and does not substitute fake production implementations.

items.title: Add required Python 3.12 CI for the supported simulation profiles
items.goal: Run meaningful checks on pull requests and main; optional AI-review automation is not a test gate.
acceptance: Run cold startup, minimal smoke, component tests, and focused graph/GOAP/event/action checks with bounded timeouts.
Use actual exit status and executed test counts; keep optional ML checks separate and visible.
Cache verified dependencies, use minimal workflow permissions, and pin external workflow actions appropriately.

items.title: Plan user journeys, controls, and understandable simulation feedback
items.goal: Define what players, observers, and contributors need to understand and control in the console and Pygame workflows.
acceptance: Map launch, observe, inspect character/building, pause, save, load, failure recovery, and exit journeys.
Specify keyboard/mouse controls, discoverability, feedback, and action/event explanations.
Define usability scenarios and success criteria to use during the Phase 8 human walkthrough.

items.title: Plan visual direction and aesthetic constraints for the village and HUD
items.goal: Choose a coherent visual direction suitable for the existing 2D Pygame runtime and available resources.
acceptance: Document palette, typography, spacing, hierarchy, icon/selection language, and map/character readability.
Specify asset provenance/licensing, resolution constraints, and legibility against map backgrounds.
Include representative visual references and human review questions; decorative effects must respect performance budgets.

items.title: Plan UI information architecture, wireframes, and interaction states
items.goal: Translate the approved user journeys and visual direction into implementable Pygame screen/panel specifications.
acceptance: Specify HUD, inspection panels, inventory/plan feedback, notifications, and supported save/load controls.
Cover idle, selected, paused, unavailable, error, saving/loading, and recovery states.
Plan configurable dimensions, focus/keyboard operation, contrast, non-color cues, and reduced-motion options where applicable.

items.title: Human design planning review: UX, UI, and visual direction
items.goal: Walk through the design artifacts and record distinct decisions about usability, interface scope, and visual direction.
acceptance: Review persona journeys and wireframes against the frozen MVP rather than unrelated web-app conventions.
Review aesthetics, text/selection contrast, supported resolutions, controls, and error feedback.
Record specific approved decisions and linked rework issues before authorizing UI implementation.

items.title: Human modern-practices review: architecture, dependencies, and CI plan
items.goal: Review the engineering foundation against Python 3.12, Pygame, and the repository's actual architecture.
acceptance: Review import boundaries, dependency/version profiles, runtime configuration, and explicit error/state contracts.
Check behavioral validation, model/service initialization, package integrity, and CI result reporting.
Document architecture decisions and scoped remediation without requiring a wholesale framework rewrite.

items.title: Triage the original issue backlog into canonical subsystem epics
items.goal: Review the original 261 issue summaries and current live backlog against code and reproduction evidence.
acceptance: Give each original item an owner, reproduction/acceptance criteria, parent topic, prerequisite, and implement/verify/duplicate/defer disposition.
Recheck apparently implemented #482/#355/#602/#596/#597/#609; do not close #602 while its regression checks are blocked.
Preserve useful historical context and require human-approved evidence before duplicate closures.

items.title: Consolidate duplicate utility changes in PRs #703 and #714
items.goal: Select one implementation of the shared is_numeric TypeError fix and combine only useful, behavior-oriented tests.
acceptance: Avoid creating two competing tests/test_tiny_util_funcs.py files.
Confirm tweener, numeric conversion, and clamping expectations reflect documented semantics.
Rebase the selected change and close/supersede the duplicate only after a maintainer decision.

items.title: Reconcile older functional-test PRs with current test locations
items.goal: Consolidate overlapping test rewrites instead of merging stale branches that restore obsolete file layouts or weaken assertions.
acceptance: Review #420/#417/#408/#406 and #404/#397/#395/#391 plus #393 against current main and merged #349.
Salvage tests that validate real behavior, actual goal completion, and graph contracts; avoid copied production logic in mocks.
Document each PR's keep/rebase/split/supersede decision and targeted validation evidence.

items.title: Reconcile PR ownership, merge sequence, and dependency configuration
items.goal: Maintain the issue-backed Project as the live execution plan after backlog triage.
acceptance: Assign a reviewer and owner to each selected implementation PR and verify current CI/mergeability.
Rebase each dependent PR after its prerequisite lands; retain existing native parents and dependency links.
Update Phase/Sequence/Readiness/Depends on and create a distinct issue for every newly discovered remediation.

items.title: Align Action.execute and the action catalog with GraphManager
items.goal: Complete the existing action-execution integration request using canonical fields, concrete preconditions, and graph propagation.
acceptance: Review PR #696 with real character/graph state, canonical aliases, and string/UUID target resolution.
Successful effects update character and graph consistently; rejected actions do not apply effects.
Use one responsible execution layer and prevent duplicate mutations or reward accounting.

items.title: Document and reconcile need/resource scales at runtime boundaries
items.goal: Resolve the current 0-1, 0-10, and 0-100 inconsistencies between demo characters, effects, graph state, and goal targets.
acceptance: Choose documented units per canonical field and explicit conversions at planner/prompt boundaries.
Validate clamps, thresholds, costs, and target effects on real scenarios.
Record representative before/after states so apparent action success cannot hide unchanged or incorrectly clamped values.

items.title: Use GOAP for valid multi-step StrategyManager plans
items.goal: Complete the StrategyManager/GOAP integration request without collapsing plans into immediate utility selection.
acceptance: Review/rebase PR #689 after action contracts and the #706 fallback repair.
Distinguish no plan from an already-satisfied goal; validate/copy simulated state and bound caching/replanning.
Show that executing a returned plan actually reaches the target state.

items.title: Execute active plans across simulation ticks and replan on failure
items.goal: Wire planner output into the actual daily character execution loop, which currently chooses the first available action.
acceptance: Track a per-character active plan/cursor and execute the intended next step at each tick.
Invalidate or replan when preconditions/world state change and hand failures back to StrategyManager.
Assert end-to-end actor identity, plan progress, goal achievement, and consistent graph state.

items.title: Complete named-target regressions against the initialized world
items.goal: Validate the existing target_character_in_location implementation after startup and execution repairs.
acceptance: All existing named-target checks finish instead of hanging in global initialization.
Co-location, requested identity, absent targets, duplicate visitor entries, and graph updates behave correctly.
Use real graph-backed state where feasible and decide #602's disposition from executed evidence.

items.title: Human contract review: actions, state units, planning, and execution
items.goal: Review a complete multi-step scenario and failure/replan path using production contracts.
acceptance: Inspect actual before/after character and graph state, not only mock call counts.
Review identity/units/preconditions/effects, cache validity, bounded failures, and plan continuation.
Record an explicit approval or linked rework before the event-integration phase.

acceptance: All phase work is tracked as individual issues.
Phase gate H5 records the human decision and evidence.
Optional/deferred work is explicitly documented and does not silently become a release prerequisite.

items.title: Route event strategy output through character-aware execution
items.goal: Complete the existing EventHandler integration request without bare action.execute calls or default-subject routing.
acceptance: Rebase PR #690 against the merged #698 payload and #699 consequence changes.
Resolve and preserve the intended actor through event, strategy, execution, and memory.
Exercise real multi-character event-to-action paths in addition to interface-level doubles.

items.title: Validate event payloads, prioritization, consequences, and scheduling
items.goal: Verify the integrated event lifecycle rather than reimplementing features already merged.
acceptance: Typed and event-like payloads trigger deterministic, bounded processing.
Priority and consequence dispatch preserve actor/location context and required order.
No duplicate handling, unbounded cascades, or unexpected cross-character effects occur.

items.title: Record event/action outcomes in memory and accounting once
items.goal: Use one post-action path for successful effects, memory, statistics, and user-facing feedback.
acceptance: Count and remember each successful action once across daily and event-driven routes.
Failed actions produce accurate failure evidence without successful reward/memory accounting.
A trace connects event, actor, selected plan, applied effect, and resulting state.

items.title: Recover subsystem failures without losing simulation state
items.goal: Address the existing recovery request with state-preserving, failure-isolated runtime behavior.
acceptance: One actor/action failure does not prevent other villagers from progressing.
Recovery does not silently rebuild away valid world state or replay applied effects.
Bound retries, preserve diagnostic cause, and verify the intended recovery with actual outcomes.

items.title: Human walkthrough: event-driven decisions and understandable feedback
items.goal: A reviewer observes an event affecting the correct villagers and checks both behavior and explanations.
acceptance: Walk through success, invalid input, actor-specific failure, and recovery.
Confirm understandable event/decision/action feedback without exposing irrelevant implementation details.
Record approval or issue-backed remediation before economic integration.

Optional/deferred work is explicitly documented and does not silently become a release prerequisite.

items.title: Add concrete item types and inventory category support
items.goal: Complete the existing item-type request with usable, consistently categorized objects.
acceptance: Review PR #695 for concrete metadata, inventory grouping, aliases, and fallback category behavior.
Item construction works under the supported core profile.
Verify quantities and interactions against real inventory operations.

items.title: Implement concrete item interactions with valid effects
items.goal: Complete the existing item-interactions request using the agreed action contracts.
acceptance: Review PR #692 after item models and Phase 4 action/state changes.
Use, equip, consume, and applicable crafting interactions enforce real requirements.
Effects change actual state and quantities without duplicated inventory mutation.

items.title: Implement job assignment, work outcomes, and career progression
items.goal: Complete the existing job-system request with operational work and measurable outcomes.
acceptance: Review PR #697 for application/assignment/leave-job, role metadata, wages, skills, production, and progression.
Use module-relative role-data paths and explicit validation for unavailable/invalid roles.
Prove one work execution produces its intended wages, costs, and goods once.

items.title: Integrate production, trade, consumption, and economic state
items.goal: Complete the existing economic-integration request as a concrete work/food loop.
acceptance: Review PR #694 after job and item contracts.
Trade conserves money and inventory; production and consumption are measurable and rate-limited.
Prevent double wages or rewards across Action, JobManager, EconomicSimulation, and controller paths.

items.title: Expose inventory needs and trade/drop choices to decisions
items.goal: Use real inventory availability in character decisions and prompt context.
acceptance: Review PR #693 against the chosen inventory and economic APIs.
Unavailable items/actions are not offered as valid choices.
Decision and prompt contexts show consistent quantities and useful choices without duplicate aliases.

items.title: Review owner-based building access and income when in scope
items.goal: Complete the existing ownership request only if the approved MVP scenario requires it.
acceptance: Review PR #691 for owner identity, access requirements, and income effects.
Apply financial effects once through canonical state paths.
Phase 2/6 reviewers explicitly activate or defer this optional task; it is not an implicit MVP prerequisite.

items.title: Demonstrate the full work-to-food-to-recovery scenario
items.goal: Run the selected villagers through the first complete useful behavior loop.
acceptance: Goals drive work, wages, food acquisition, eating, and recovery rather than name-based fake wealth increments.
Different needs/scarcity produce explainable changes in chosen actions.
Verify actor/graph/inventory state and conserved totals over multiple ticks.

items.title: Human review: economic behavior, balance, and data integrity
items.goal: Review the scenario outcomes and whether they produce a believable and understandable village loop.
acceptance: Walk through success, insufficient money, unavailable goods, and failed work/trade.
Inspect wage/item conservation, meaningful need changes, and the scope decision for ownership.
Record approved tuning/behavior or create specific remediation issues.

items.title: Define versioned snapshots and atomic save behavior
items.goal: Create a supported state contract before expanding the current partial loader.
acceptance: Specify stable IDs, schema version, world/actor state, inventories, relationships, events, time, and supported memory data.
Validate input before replacing live state and write saves atomically.
Document incompatible/corrupt save handling and supported migrations.

items.title: Restore map, buildings, and world entities by stable ID
items.goal: Complete the existing world-restoration request before recreating dependent actors.
acceptance: Restore required world/building state and item locations.
Use stable identity so subsequent character and relationship restoration resolves correctly.
Validate missing/incompatible world references without partial silent success.

items.title: Restore complete supported character state and inventory
items.goal: Complete the existing character-restoration request instead of returning success without restoring actors.
acceptance: Restore supported attributes, positions/locations, inventory, jobs, goals, and plan progress.
Rebind restored objects to the authoritative graph and world entities.
Verify saved values actually replace the running state.

items.title: Restore relationships and graph-backed social state
items.goal: Complete the existing relationship-restoration request rather than only logging that data was present.
acceptance: Rebuild relationships against restored actor/world IDs.
Controller and graph read/write the same authoritative relationship state.
Validate invalid/missing references and preserve supported relationship attributes.

items.title: Restore economic state and production/trade bookkeeping
items.goal: Complete the existing economic-state restoration request.
acceptance: Restore supported balances, availability, job assignments, production state, and rate-limit bookkeeping.
Restart does not duplicate wages, production, or already applied trades.
Verify the next economic tick agrees with an equivalent uninterrupted simulation.

items.title: Persist basic memory records, pending events, time, and randomness
items.goal: Preserve the core simulation's continuation state while keeping model/index persistence explicitly separate.
acceptance: Restore supported plain memory records and pending event/plan state.
Preserve simulation time and deterministic RNG state needed by the approved scenario.
Document that full NLP/FAISS model/index persistence is addressed separately by #614 in Phase 9.

items.title: Validate restart/load continuation and corrupted saves
items.goal: Prove persistence works by comparing actual resulting simulation state.
acceptance: Save, restart, load, and continue produce equivalent state and subsequent behavior.
Missing/invalid/version-mismatched data fail clearly before mutating valid live state.
Verify restored actor/graph/inventory identities and no double application of events or rewards.

items.title: Human review: save/load correctness and recoverability
items.goal: Walk through supported save/load journeys and their failure feedback.
acceptance: Review snapshot versions, actual restored values, identity consistency, and corruption behavior.
Inspect user-facing recovery instructions and ensure errors do not conceal partial restores.
Record approval or linked remediation before release-facing UI validation.

items.goal: Complete the existing MVP-documentation request using current behavior instead of unsupported readiness claims.
acceptance: Refresh PRs #687/#688 and reconcile README, Quickstart, status/reference docs, and Memory Bank.
Remove generated session/audit logs from documentation changes and contextualize archived claims.
Document the same commands, optional features, actual failures, and support matrix everywhere.

items.title: Freeze and document the canonical deterministic MVP demo
items.goal: Complete the existing MVP-path issue, including its implementation and documentation criteria.
acceptance: One official command runs fixed villagers, world, events, and seed under the supported profile.
Document what users will see and how to reproduce it from scratch.
The demo exhibits real integrated behavior and reports a verifiable final summary.

items.title: Explain goals, decisions, events, and outcomes in demo feedback
items.goal: Complete the existing narrative-log clarity issue.
acceptance: Explain why a villager chose an action and how events/needs influenced it.
Report successful, failed, recovered, and deferred outcomes accurately.
Keep implementation details out of ordinary product feedback unless needed for a user decision.

items.title: Implement the approved MVP UI and UX specification
items.goal: Apply the Phase 2 human-approved interaction and visual plans to the supported Pygame/console surfaces.
acceptance: Implement agreed HUD/inspection/notification/control and save/load feedback behavior.
Provide legible selection, focus, paused/error/recovery states and supported-resolution handling.
Review PR #710 for graceful map-render failure feedback; track discovered UI fixes as separate linked issues.

items.title: Measure MVP stability, frame times, memory, and failure recovery
items.goal: Use existing performance instrumentation to establish evidence for release readiness.
acceptance: Run the fixed scenario, then a bounded multi-villager soak using the Phase 2 budgets.
Record frame/decision timings, memory growth, crashes, stuck plans, and recovery behavior.
Create issues for actionable findings; verify #596/#597 from evidence instead of duplicating implemented instrumentation.

items.title: Human aesthetic review of the village, HUD, and visual states
items.goal: Judge visual coherence and readability against the approved direction using actual captured screens.
acceptance: Review palette, typography, spacing, hierarchy, map/character legibility, and selection/error visual language.
Check supported resolutions/backgrounds and asset consistency/provenance.
Record approved visual decisions or individual remediation issues with examples.

items.title: Human UX usability walkthrough of all supported MVP journeys
items.goal: Observe users/reviewers completing the agreed journeys without inventing successful usability results.
acceptance: Walk through launch, observe, inspect, pause, save/load, recover, and exit.
Check discoverability, feedback timing, narrative clarity, and meaningful user control.
Record observations, friction, approved decisions, and issue-backed fixes.

items.title: Human UI interaction and state consistency review
items.goal: Review the functioning interface, its controls, and its integration with simulation state.
acceptance: Verify panels, controls, labels, state transitions, and unavailable/error states.
Ensure displayed needs, inventory, goals, and save/load outcomes match authoritative state.
Review resolution/layout behavior and record required fixes separately.

items.title: Human accessibility and inclusive-interaction review
items.goal: Assess accessibility expectations appropriate to the Pygame/console surfaces.
acceptance: Check text/selection contrast, non-color status cues, readable sizes, keyboard operation, and focus visibility.
Review configurable controls, motion settings where applicable, and actionable error/recovery feedback.
Document platform constraints honestly; do not claim browser/ARIA support for a Pygame interface.

acceptance: Review cold startup, state contracts, behavioral test results, bounds/caches, configuration, and error handling.
Confirm design/UX/UI/accessibility decisions and performance results are recorded.
Verify reproducible commands, clean changes, optional-feature boundaries, and any remaining release blockers.

items.title: Phase 9: Expand optional features deliberately
items.goal: Post-MVP social, memory, LLM, and graphics increments have verified fallbacks and an explicit human release decision.
acceptance: All phase work is tracked as individual issues.
Phase gate H9 records the human decision and evidence.
Optional/deferred work is explicitly documented and does not silently become a release prerequisite.

items.title: Implement meaningful graph-backed relationship dynamics
items.goal: Complete the existing social-interaction dynamics issue after MVP release approval.
acceptance: Interactions change relationships through the authoritative graph.
State changes reflect actual outcomes and remain consistent after save/load.
Validate success/failure behavior and human-readable social consequences.

items.title: Make relationships influence character decisions
items.goal: Complete the existing relationship-aware decision issue.
acceptance: Relationship context changes goal selection, ranking, or planning in explainable scenarios.
Preserve the stable non-LLM runtime path.
Verify effects on real behavior rather than only prompt substrings.

items.title: Use memory and relationship summaries in actual decisions
items.goal: Complete the existing memory-to-decision integration issue with scoped, current-code changes.
acceptance: Review PR #363 for stale/unrelated changes before selecting its useful parts.
Memory/relationship data influence real prompt/planning decisions and optional absence degrades gracefully.
Validate retrieval context, relevance, and supported memory records without mock-only success.

items.title: Harden structured LLM output parsing and fallback behavior
items.goal: Complete the existing robust-output issue against the supported Action contracts.
acceptance: Validate schema, parameters, identity, allowed actions, and malformed/unknown responses.
Reject invalid output and retain a meaningful deterministic fallback.
Verify real parser-to-action behavior without weakening assertions.

items.title: Bound model, memory, cache, and index resource usage
items.goal: Complete the existing MemoryManager resource-management request before expanding model-enabled usage.
acceptance: Measure and bound model instances, retrieval caches, and index lifecycle.
Use owned cache configuration and explicit initialization/cleanup instead of repeated import-time loading.
Verify long-running behavior and preserve artifact/TLS verification.

items.title: Persist or rebuild supported NLP and memory indexes
items.goal: Complete the existing full memory-persistence request beyond the basic Phase 7 snapshot.
acceptance: Persist supported memory records/index metadata and reliably rebuild indexes after restart.
Do not serialize entire live model objects as the save format.
Verify equivalent retrieval/decision behavior after load and documented version compatibility.

items.title: Implement strategic and bounded LLM invocation
items.goal: Complete the existing strategic invocation issue after memory/resource safeguards are ready.
acceptance: Review criteria for crisis/social/novelty/explicit requests and preserve routine non-LLM behavior.
Review PR #709 helpers and #711 diagnostics where relevant.
Document provider/model choice, timeouts, budgets, and secure prerequisites before any live inference.

items.title: Trace LLM calls, reasons, outcomes, and fallbacks
items.goal: Complete the existing LLM observability request.
acceptance: Each invocation/fallback records actor, trigger, goal, outcome, and bounded timing.
Avoid credential or unnecessary personal-data logging.
Connect diagnostics to the supported user-facing behavior and review evidence.

items.title: Verify strategic LLM paths with meaningful integration evidence
items.goal: Complete the existing strategic-LLM testing request.
acceptance: Cover routine/crisis/social/explicit request/failure fallback paths using real parser/strategy contracts.
Keep live-model checks separate from deterministic core CI and report their executed results honestly.
Prove model/service unavailability cannot break the approved MVP.

items.title: Validate weighted pathfinding correctness before optimizing queues
items.goal: Complete the existing pathfinding robustness request and review PR #712's priority-update risk.
acceptance: An improved route to an already-queued node updates the effective heap priority or safely adds a fresh entry.
Verify weighted optimal paths, unreachable goals, obstacles, and stale entries.
Benchmark only after correctness is established.

items.title: Add scoped anti-aliasing consistent with visual and performance budgets
items.goal: Complete the existing anti-aliasing request only after the stable rendering baseline.
acceptance: Review PR #713 against approved visual direction and current render/map code.
Validate configuration/toggle behavior and supported visual surfaces.
Measure frame-time impact and retain an explicit fallback/disable option.

items.title: Human disposition review of optional tooling and experimental PRs
items.goal: Keep contributor tooling and experimental modules separate from the product delivery path.
acceptance: Record keep/separate/defer/supersede decisions for #705/#707/#708/#592/#702/#700.
Treat AI Algorithm Mentor as optional automation with distinct permission/provider prerequisites, not required test CI.
Do not ship generated dummy fixtures, unrelated LangGraph tooling, or experimental sleep changes as MVP runtime work.

items.title: Human review of optional feature behavior and operational readiness
items.goal: Review the selected post-MVP capabilities before treating them as supported product behavior.
acceptance: Review social/memory/LLM fallbacks, persistence, instrumentation, budgets, and rendering correctness.
Run the unchanged supported MVP as a regression control.
Record remaining deferred increments and approval/rework decisions with evidence.

items.title: Human decision gate 9: Expand optional features deliberately
items.goal: A human maintainer decides whether the phase satisfies its acceptance criteria and may unlock the next phase.
acceptance: Review every required task, current PR head, commands/results, and the phase-specific evidence.
Walk through the supported behavior, failure cases, and applicable design/engineering artifacts.
Choose exactly Approved, Changes requested, or Deferred; record reviewer, date, rationale, evidence, and issue-backed remediation.
Only close this gate after a human records Approved; keep rework/deferred gates open and downstream work blocked.
Do not auto-approve based on a passing suite, a bot action, elapsed time, or a completed checklist.
